observedEvidence.name: Bone Knight - Horned Skull Greatsword
observations: Front/side/rear views show actual rib and narrow spine-waist openings between shoulder/back plate and pelvis armor; exposed long bones and bony fingers/toes preserve negative space.
Skull has deep eye/nasal apertures, separate lower jaw and irregular teeth; horns emerge from temporal skull regions rather than arbitrary helmet cones.
Layered dark corroded plate, thick rims/rivets and pale aged bone/spikes remain materially distinct; side view shows the actual depth of shoulder and forearm assemblies.
Armor bridges over a skeleton and remains open at the waist. There is no continuous living flesh or opaque intact tunic filling those skeletal openings.
boundaries: Approved units require small recessed green eye glow, rusty dark/gold kit and torn violet textiles, plus spear/bow/halberd distinctions. The reference greatsword and skull horns must not replace all role targets.

Advertised CC BY4/downloadable but static 1.96M faces; no archive, rig, UV, acquired asset or source rights review has occurred.

observedEvidence.name: Test Orc Head
observations: Face closeup/profile show a projecting lower dental arcade, thick lower lip/chin and embedded uneven lower tusks/teeth. The mouth is a recessed opening bounded by lips, not a flat black strip.
Low folded brow, upper/lower lid folds, nasal wings and deep diagonal cheek-to-mouth folds create transitions into a heavy jaw and thick neck. Wrinkles track the underlying volumes.
Ear has a thick cupped rim, internal folds and a broad connected root; both three-quarter angles confirm depth, rather than an attached triangle.
The rear/bust underside is simplified, and the profile shows a tall bald cranium. Those parts are not evidence of a complete soldier/body mesh.
boundaries: The Peris Orc has a lower, narrower head relative to huge shoulders, less age/droop, a squarer jaw and a black topknot. Preserve that portrait proportion; do not copy this tall bald dome or rounded old chin.
Use the observed projecting lip/jaw, eye recess and nested folds to replace block/balloon forms. Keep smaller upward lower-jaw tusks, not downward cheek fangs.
No reuse license, downloadable source, rig, UV or archive rights are established.

observedEvidence.name: Elf Warrior
observations: Both sides/full-body views show long narrow limbs and torso. Curved fluted/leaf plate ridges flow through helmet, pauldrons, chest, waist lames and greaves with real layered thickness.

Continuous dark flexible leather/fabric fills plate gaps; mesh/mail-patterned flex zones remain visible at elbows and behind thigh/waist plates. Waist lames overlap over an underlayer instead of exposing holes.

Back view shows articulated back plates and the soft layer continuing into the hip/leg seams. Shoulder caps, bracers and greaves have separate edging and coverage rather than one painted body surface.
Helmet covers the ears and much of the face. No weapon appears; the arms are in a rig construction A-pose.
boundaries: Use layered plate/flexible-underlayer construction and narrow proportions. The approved portrait requires green/silver leaf kit, long blond hair and mostly open face/visible ears, not this closed gold helmet.
Helmet filigree is not bare ear anatomy. A-pose does not establish combat stance, hand grips, cloth simulation or animation clearance.
Viewer-only; no reuse license/archive is established.

acceptanceSequence.required: Inspect and rotate 2-3 strong references per race. Record observed face/body, construction, cloth/armor/material and pose findings; resolve listed knowledge gaps.
Build one convincing portrait-matched complete hero first, starting with Orc. Judge actual face/body/armor/weapon contact under neutral lighting and actual game inspection.

Review all nine roles together at the same camera/scale. Head/body/coverage/weapon/pose/mount or machine must create deliberate differences; small recolors/accessories do not establish nine distinct roles.
Sample idle, locomotion and appropriate attack/throw/ram clips. Check feet, saddle/pelvis, reins, grip/string/arrow and armor contacts in side/back views.
Show major improvements as screenshots; compare close inspection and battle overview under game lighting, including shadows and LOD. Do not label a unit finished until its racial and role gates pass.
Preserve editable source, UV/material detail, legal attribution and source hashes; validate role inventory and clips, then measure actual battle cost. Tests cannot substitute for visual approval.

observations: Front and rear views show a small head between very broad trapezius/deltoids, large forearms/hands and short bowed legs; rear scapula/lat volumes are part of the connected torso.

directViewerStudies.name: Test Orc Head
observations: Face closeup/profile show a projecting lower dental arcade, thick lower lip/chin and embedded uneven lower tusks/teeth. The mouth is a recessed opening bounded by lips, not a flat black strip.
Low folded brow, upper/lower lid folds, nasal wings and deep diagonal cheek-to-mouth folds create transitions into a heavy jaw and thick neck. Wrinkles track the underlying volumes.
Ear has a thick cupped rim, internal folds and a broad connected root; both three-quarter angles confirm depth, rather than an attached triangle.
The rear/bust underside is simplified, and the profile shows a tall bald cranium. Those parts are not evidence of a complete soldier/body mesh.
portraitComparison: The Peris Orc has a lower, narrower head relative to huge shoulders, less age/droop, a squarer jaw and a black topknot. Preserve that portrait proportion; do not copy this tall bald dome or rounded old chin.
Use the observed projecting lip/jaw, eye recess and nested folds to replace block/balloon forms. Keep smaller upward lower-jaw tusks, not downward cheek fangs.
No reuse license, downloadable source, rig, UV or archive rights are established.

armorUnderlayerStudy: Infer from Tanker and the approved portrait that straps/lining support each shoulder/cuirass piece; preserve exposed huge upper arms rather than fill every gap with plate.

Fur cuffs/boots and leather wraps have volume and contact; they cannot hide poorly shaped wrists/feet or replace hand anatomy.

directViewerStudies.name: Demon Warrior & Axes of Agony
observations: Front/surface detail and rear show connected organic ridges over chest/abdomen/shoulders, integrated back/limb spines and rough pale shell around visibly red soft-tissue seams.
A single eye is inside a tooth-lined mouth-like head; spiky crown/skull and nude shell biology define this specific character, not ordinary separate forged torso armor.
Long forearms and taloned feet have anatomical transitions into ridges/claws. Axe ornament is rough while the exposed cutting edge has a sharper metal highlight.
Side/rear confirm limb/foot and back depth; static display arm pose and grasp do not establish a combat/mounted animation rig.
portraitComparison: Do not literally transfer cyclops mouth/eye, pale exoskeleton, exposed red body seams or twin axes to all units. Our Div portraits have two eyes, a red angular face, curved dark ridged horns and crafted charcoal/copper plate with red cloth.
Use connected anatomy, spine roots and differentiated shell/soft tissue/metal principles, adapting to portrait skin/horn/obsidian materials.
Source displays CC BY4/downloadable, but login was required and no archive was acquired. UVs, rig, topology, source rights and actual animations remain unverified.
Static face/body references do not establish horned wolf/rhino saddle fit or giant boulder contact.

directViewerStudies.name: The Balrog of Moria
observations: Side/rear silhouettes show a broad monster upper body, bent powerful legs, long clawed hands, curved tail and membrane wings connected across the shoulder/back region.

The close image labeled torso wing root detail actually crops most of the head: visible evidence mainly concerns pectoral/abdominal masses, wing-root depth, long claws, rough dark hide and orange fissures.
Bright fire/blade glow and very dark lighting hide much of the face, horn root and material detail. Tiny silhouette views are not a precise facial anatomy or neutral texture reference.
portraitComparison: Recognizable LOTR Balrog character, wings/tail/fire weapons and reuse/provenance rights are unresolved. No literal character import, viewer extraction or copy into Peris.
Our original Shahnameh Div portraits specify no large wings/fire effects hiding bodies, two-eyed red angular faces, crafted obsidian/copper armor and role-specific weapons. Preserve those targets.
Use broad silhouette, connected monstrous limb mass and organic attachment principles only; these saved angles do not approve detailed horn/eye/face shapes.
No downloadable archive/acquired asset, rig or Three.js cost evidence.
